comments.author: @BestGlobalTravelDocumentary
comments.text: What impressed me most about Molokai is how it has managed to preserve its simple way of life and unique culture despite Hawaii becoming such a popular tourist destination. The breathtaking cliffs, ancient fishponds, and the way locals stay connected to their land and traditions really stood out to me. It’s a reminder that a place’s true beauty isn’t just in its scenery, but also in the people and the values they hold on to. Really enjoyed this documentary!

comments.author: @EvervistaTravel66
comments.text: The words "money can't buy" are what make this title interesting. At first, they sound like a promise of an exclusive destination. But they also raise a more meaningful question: what about a place should never be reduced to a price tag? A coastline can be photographed and a vacation can be booked, but a community's sense of home isn't something a visitor can purchase. That's the story I'd most want to understand.
